validity.recommendation: No action on existence/classification. See separate attribution, duplicate, and spec flags below for this same row.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: real, independently corroborated project. Traced the sheet's own two citations to their origin: dostor.org/4487576 (29-Aug-2023) reports on a PPC community-consultation/EIA session for 'replacement and renewal of the Beni Suef/Asyut petroleum-products line, 16-inch diameter, 75 km' (بقطر 16 بوصة بطول 75 كم) -- exact match on length+diameter. Found the PRIMARY source dostor was reporting on: Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum's OWN official page (petroleum.gov.eg /environment-safety/social-meetings/...), dated 29/08/2023, titled for this exact joint session -- confirms PPC held the EIA consultation for 'design, construction and operation of: the Beni Suef/Asyut products line, 16in, 75km ... and the El-Tebeen/Asyut products line, 12in, 20km in Minya' (the second project = P7326, also confirmed in passing). The sheet's other cited ref (petro-mag.org, PPC's own in-house 'Petroleum' magazine, December 2024 edition) is a page-flip viewer that url_verifier cannot text-search (large embedded PDF -- documented tool limitation); I pulled the underlying PDF directly (petro-mag.org/Uploads/Files/1db11fff-b2e2-445c-aa2f-a1c78dbd7c9b.pdf, 146pp) and confirmed via pdftotext that p.138 lists this same project twice: once under 'EIA studies -- (11) environmental approvals obtained from EEAA', item 8, 'replacement/renewal of part of the Beni Suef/Asyut products line, 16in, 75km', and once under 'Replacement & Renewal Projects', 'replacement/renewal of part of the 12in El-Tebeen/Asyut products line TO 16in diameter, 75km -- purpose: to secure and raise delivery rates of petroleum products between El-Tebeen and Asyut'. So the project is real, still being tracked by PPC 16 months after the 2023 EIA session, and length (75km) + diameter (16in, the NEW/upgraded diameter) are corroborated across three PPC-chain sources (Ministry primary page, dostor, PPC's own magazine). Fuel = 'Oil products (only)' matches every source's 'منتجات بترولية' (petroleum products, refined). PipelineType = transmission is correct: this is a multi-governorate refined-products trunk line, not a gathering/feeder line. Minor unrelated observation: Owner1=Egyptian General Petroleum Corp 100% is sourced only to a generic EGPC 'About' page, not a project-specific ownership document -- this is the standard pattern across nearly every EGPC-attributed row in this scope (PPC is an EGPC subsidiary) and not a defect unique to this row, so I did not flag it separately.

validity.recommendation: Not a data-entry duplicate of P7334 (El-Tibeen-Asyut Oil Products Pipeline, 376 km, 12/16in, operating) -- but P7325 is specifically a REPLACEMENT/UPGRADE of a ~75 km piece of that same 376 km corridor (diameter going 12in -> 16in on that stretch), not new incremental route. Flag for a human decision at the point P7325 reaches 'operating': either shorten/adjust P7334's LengthKnown or diameter breakdown for the overlapping stretch, or otherwise cross-reference the two rows in ResearcherNotes, so the corridor's total length/capacity isn't double-counted once the replacement pipe is in service.
validity.researcher_notes: PPC's own December-2024 magazine (petro-mag.org PDF, p.138, 'Replacement & Renewal Projects' section) describes this exact 75km/16in project as 'إحالل وتجديد جزء من خط 12" منتجات التبين/أسيوط إلى قطر 16" بطول 75 كم' -- literally 'replacement/renewal of PART of the 12in El-Tebeen/Asyut products line, TO 16in diameter, 75km'. That is explicitly a rebuild of a segment of the El-Tebeen-Asyut corridor -- the same corridor P7334 tracks as a completed 376km/12,16in operating line. Corroborating history: a 2019 youm7.com article (verified) itemizing PPC's Upper-Egypt pipeline program states the El-Tebeen-Asyut line was completed at 376km (item 9), then duplicated in two phases -- El-Tebeen/Asyut to Beni Suef, 112km (phase 1) and Beni Suef to Minya, 146km (phase 2) -- confirming the corridor's mixed-diameter, multi-phase-build history that P7334's '12,16' diameter field already reflects. P7325 is the NEXT lifecycle event on part of that same corridor (an aging-pipe replacement, not a duplication/capacity add), so once it reaches 'operating' the two rows will describe overlapping physical territory unless reconciled.

validity.recommendation: Verify/likely correct EndState/Province and EndLocation. Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum's own official page for this exact project states its physical scope as running 'from valve chamber 15 to valve chamber 18, IN MINYA governorate' (من غرفة بلوف 15 حتى غرفة بلوف 18 بالمنيا) -- the actual endpoint of this specific 75km segment is a facility in Minya governorate, not Asyut city/governorate. Recommend changing EndState/Province to Minya (exact settlement/facility for chamber 18 not identified in sources found) pending confirmation; StartLocation=Beni Suef is plausible (chamber 15's governorate is not explicitly stated in any source found -- could still be within Beni Suef near its Minya border) and I am not recommending a change there without more.
validity.researcher_notes: The pipeline's colloquial/brand name ('Beni Suef/Asyut products line') is what both PPC and the press use for this project and appears to be inherited from the broader corridor's historical naming rather than describing this specific 75km segment's literal endpoints. The Ministry of Petroleum's own social-meetings page (petroleum.gov.eg, dated 29-Aug-2023, primary/authoritative -- this is the actual source dostor.org's article is reporting on) is explicit: the EIA covered 'design, construction and operation of the Beni Suef/Asyut petroleum-products line, 16in, 75km, FROM VALVE CHAMBER 15 TO VALVE CHAMBER 18 IN MINYA' and, in the same session, the separate El-Tebeen/Asyut 12in/20km line 'FROM VALVE CHAMBER 18 to the Cooperative Society IN MINYA' (=P7326, whose own GEM endpoint IS correctly recorded as El Minya). Chamber 18 is thus confirmed in Minya governorate for BOTH projects discussed in that session, and it is P7325's own stated end point. This does not reach Asyut governorate/city at all as far as sourced. GEM's current EndState/Province='Asyut' for P7325 looks like it inherited the corridor's overall destination (the wider El-Tebeen-Asyut trunk does terminate in Asyut) rather than this specific segment's actual scope.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify Status. Both sources the sheet itself cites for Status='construction' actually describe an EARLIER lifecycle stage than construction: dostor.org (Aug-2023) reports only a community-consultation/EIA STUDY session, and PPC's own Dec-2024 magazine lists this project among '(11) EIA approvals OBTAINED from EEAA' (i.e., environmental permitting cleared) -- neither states that physical construction/pipe-laying has begun. No source found (including a further web search) confirms groundbreaking. If no newer construction-specific source exists, 'proposed' (per the tracker's proposed->construction->operating vocabulary) may be the more defensible current Status; if a source exists that was used to set Status='construction' as of the 2026-01-28 update, it was not among the two cited refs and should be added.
validity.researcher_notes: Sequence established from the sheet's own two Status citations plus the primary source behind the first: (1) 29-Aug-2023, Ministry of Petroleum's own page + dostor.org: PPC holds an EIA community-consultation session for this project ('تقييم الأثر البيئي' -- environmental impact STUDY, pre-permitting). (2) December-2024 PPC in-house magazine (petro-mag.org PDF p.138): this project appears in a list headed 'تم الحصول على (11) موافقة بيئية من جهاز شئون البيئة' (11 environmental approvals OBTAINED from EEAA) as item 8 -- i.e. permitting/approval stage, not construction. I could not find any later (2025-2026) source reporting a contractor mobilizing, groundbreaking, or pipe-laying for this specific 75km/16in Beni Suef-Asyut segment despite targeted Arabic searches. Separately, mechanical note: the Status[ref] cell in the sheet currently stores the two source URLs comma-joined in a single string ('https://www.dostor.org/4487576, https://petro-mag.org/...') which fails url_verifier as one malformed URL even though each resolves fine individually -- worth splitting into two distinct citations if/when this cell is next touched.

summary: P7325 is a real, well-corroborated PPC replacement/upgrade project (Beni Suef/Asyut products line, 12in->16in, 75km) confirmed via the sheet's own citations traced to their Ministry-of-Petroleum primary source plus PPC's own Dec-2024 magazine; existence/Fuel/PipelineType confirmed. Three flags: (1) duplicate/caveat -- it rebuilds part of P7334's 376km corridor, watch for double-counted length once operating; (2) attribution concern -- the Ministry's own page places the segment's actual endpoint (valve chamber 18) in MINYA governorate, not Asyut as currently recorded; (3) spec/status concern -- both cited sources describe only EIA-study/approval stage, not confirmed physical construction, so Status='construction' is unverified by its own refs.
